items.title: Asking about a flat to rent

tx.t: Cityside Properties, good morning.
I'm interested in the flat in Old Town.
Yes, it has two bedrooms. The rent is four hundred and fifty pounds a month.
And is there a deposit?
Yes, the deposit is seven hundred and fifty pounds. Would you like to view it?
Yes, please.
I can show you around on Tuesday at twenty to four. Could I take your name?
Hassan Lindqvist, spelled L, I, N, D, Q, V, I, S, T. My number is oh seven one three five three five oh seven oh three.

qs.q: Which area is the flat in?

tx.t: Hello, community office.
I'd like to register for the community music evening.
Lovely. It takes place on the seventh of April at ten to one.
Where is it being held?
At the old school. It costs eight pounds per person.
I'd like to register two people.
No problem. And your name?
Ingrid Abbott, that's A, B, B, O, T, T.

qs.q: Which event does the caller want to join?
What is the date of the event?

tx.t: Good morning, Greenfield Leisure Centre. How can I help?
Hello, I'd like to join the gym. Could you tell me about membership?
Of course. Could I take your name first?
It's Zara Chaudhry. That's C, H, A, U, D, H, R, Y.
Thank you. A standard membership is forty-five pounds a month, and there is a joining fee of twenty pounds.
Does that include the swimming pool?
Yes, the pool is included, but yoga classes cost an extra six pounds each. The gym is open from half past seven until ten to nine on weekdays.
Great. I'll come in on Friday to sign the form. What should I bring?
Please bring photo identification and proof of address. Your membership code will be V, L, six, eight, four.

qs.q: How much is the monthly membership?
What time does the gym close on weekdays?

tx.t: Hillcrest Surgery, good morning.
Hello, I'd like to make an appointment, please.
Of course. Could I have your name?
Marcus Osborne. That's O, S, B, O, R, N, E.
Thank you. Dr Fitzgerald has an appointment on Tuesday at twenty to five. Would that suit you?
Yes, that's fine. Where is the surgery exactly?
It's at eighty-five, Church Lane. Please arrive ten minutes early.
And should I give you a phone number?
Yes, please.
It is oh seven eight nine oh five four nine one oh two.

qs.q: Which street is the surgery on?

tx.t: Hello, I think I left my umbrella on the number twenty-one bus yesterday.
Can you describe it?
It's dark green, and quite old.
And what time did you get off the bus?
At about ten to two, at the hospital stop.
Let me check the shelf. Yes, I think we have it. Could I take your surname and a phone number?
It's Underwood, that's U, N, D, E, R, W, O, O, D. And my number is oh seven five six two eight three one two seven three.
Thank you. You can collect it from the main office any day before ten to six. There is a handling charge of five pounds.

qs.q: Where did the caller get off?
How much is the handling charge?

tx.t: Good evening, can I help you?
Yes, I would like two tickets for Across the Ice on Wednesday, please.
There is a showing at quarter past nine. Would that be all right?
Yes. How much is it?
Each ticket is three pounds thirty-five. I can give you seats in row H.
That is fine.
Could I have a name for the booking?
Gallagher, spelled G, A, L, L, A, G, H, E, R.
Your reference is S, G, five, three, one. Please collect the tickets twenty minutes before the film.

qs.q: Which film does the customer choose?
Which row are the seats in?

tx.t: Ridgeway Sports Shop, good afternoon.
Hello. I'm calling about the delivery driver position.
Yes, it is still open. It is fourteen hours a week, including weekends.
What is the pay?
It is ten pounds sixty an hour. We would like someone to start on the third of November.
Who should I send my application to?
To the manager, Liam Lindqvist. That is L, I, N, D, Q, V, I, S, T. Or you can ring her on oh seven seven three six nine oh three two nine four.
Hello. How can I help?
I'd like to join the library, please.
Of course. I just need a few details. What is your name?
Ben Hargreaves. That's H, A, R, G, R, E, A, V, E, S.
And your address?
eighteen, Elm Grove.
Thank you. You can borrow five books at a time for four weeks.
What happens if I return a book late?
The fine is zero pounds seventy-five a day. Your card will be ready on Wednesday.

qs.q: Which street does the member live on?
How many books can be borrowed at once?

tx.t: Hello, Parkway Learning Centre. Can I help you?
Yes, I'd like to enrol on the creative writing course, please.
Certainly. It runs for ten weeks, every Sunday evening, starting at five o'clock. The fee is one hundred and twenty pounds.
Where does the class take place?
In room eleven. Your tutor will be Chloe Mahmood.
That sounds good. My name is Liam Yardley.
Could you spell your surname?
It's Y, A, R, D, L, E, Y.
Thank you. I'll send a confirmation email today.

qs.q: Which course does the caller choose?

tx.t: Sunrise Tours, good morning.
I'd like to book two places on the trip to the Cotswolds, please.
Which date would you like?
On the eighteenth of December.
Yes, we have space. The price is forty-five pounds per person. The coach leaves at ten past eight from the town hall.
Is lunch included?
No, but there is a cafe at the first stop. Could I take your name and number?
Alice Gallagher, that's G, A, L, L, A, G, H, E, R. My number is oh seven eight two one four five three four seven nine.

qs.q: What is the date of the trip?
Where does the coach leave from?

tx.t: Welcome to our open day at Oakfield Academy. The day starts at eleven o'clock and finishes at twenty past four.
Tours of the building leave from the music room at half past one. If you want to see the classrooms, please join the first group.
Lessons cost one hundred and fifty pounds a term. You can get here by bus number thirty-two, which stops outside the gate. Our next open day is on the twelfth of November.

qs.q: When does the open day finish?
Where do the tours leave from?
When is the next open day?

tx.t: Welcome to Eastbridge College. I will tell you the most important things in the next few minutes.

The library is open until half past eight on weekdays, and until three o'clock on Sundays. Silent study is on the second floor. To borrow books, you need your student card, which you can collect from room forty-five on Tuesday.

There are more than eighty-three clubs and societies, and you can join them at the careers office. Joining one costs twenty pounds for the whole year. The careers office also runs free workshops, so please sign up early.

qs.q: What time does the library close on weekdays?
Which day can cards be collected?

tx.t: Thank you for coming to the introduction to our volunteering programme. This term we have a food bank.
It takes place every Friday at twenty past two and lasts about three hours. We need about thirty-two volunteers to make it work.
You should wear or bring a water bottle. If you would like to join, speak to Hannah Gallagher after this talk, or ring oh seven nine two three four seven eight eight one seven.

qs.q: On which day does it take place? ____
Who should interested people speak to? (surname) ____

tx.t: Thank you for calling Fairview Dental Practice. Our opening hours are quarter past nine to twenty past four from Monday to Friday, and quarter past nine to three o'clock on Saturdays. We are closed on Sundays.
We will also be closed on the first of April for the public holiday.
If you want to speak to the office, press seven. For other enquiries, call back on oh seven six two five four six oh four two five, or look at the notice board for more information.

qs.q: When does the place open on weekdays?
When does it close on weekdays?
What time does it close on Saturdays? ____
Which date is it closed for a holiday?
Number to press for the office: ____
Where can callers find more information?

tx.t: Good morning, shoppers, and welcome to Kingsgate Mall. Our end of season sale starts today, with up to forty-five per cent off in the bookshop, on the ground floor.
Everyone who spends more than seventy pounds today receives a free gift voucher worth ten pounds. Please collect it from the information desk.
Parking is free for the first three hours, and the centre closes at twenty to nine tonight.

qs.q: How much must customers spend to get a voucher?
When does the centre close tonight?

tx.t: This is a message for members of Westgate Leisure. Please note some changes to our timetable.
From next week, the children's gymnastics will move from Tuesday to Thursday, and will start at twenty past four. They will take place in the sports hall.
Because of repair work, the main pool will be closed for five weeks. During this time, entry to the gym costs twelve pounds less.
Finally, the centre will now close at quarter to eleven on weekdays. Thank you for your understanding.

qs.q: Which day will it move to?
How long will the pool be closed (weeks)? ____
What time will the centre close on weekdays?

tx.t: Attention please. The train to Leeds, which was due to leave at quarter to twelve, is delayed by about twenty-five minutes because of a signalling fault. We apologise for the delay.
This train will now depart from platform eleven. Passengers for Oxford should change at the next stop. A replacement bus will wait opposite platform one.
Passengers who are delayed by more than half an hour may claim a refund of thirty pounds at the ticket office. Thank you for your patience.

qs.q: Where is the delayed train going?
Which platform will the train leave from? ____
Where will the replacement bus wait?

tx.t: Welcome to the guided walk through Hollin Woods. We will meet at the old bridge at quarter past eleven.
The route is ten kilometres long and takes about three hours with stops. On the way, you may see owls, especially near the river.
Please remember to bring a packed lunch. The walk costs fourteen pounds per person, and you can pay at the end.

qs.q: Where does the walk take place?

o: the car park by the lake

qs.q: What time does the walk start?

tx.t: Good afternoon and welcome to the City Art Gallery. We will start in the entrance hall, where you can see a model of the town as it looked two hundred years ago.
Then we move to the ground floor, which tells the story of the Roman remains. Please do not touch the objects, even though some of them look sturdy.
The cafe is beside the entrance, and anyone with a tour ticket gets seventeen per cent off. The tour lasts about eighty-four minutes, and we will have a short break at eleven o'clock.
Photography is allowed everywhere except the temporary gallery, where flash damages the old prints. Please stay with the group, because some doors lock behind us.

qs.q: What does the exhibition on the ground floor describe?
Discount with a tour ticket (per cent): ____
How long does the tour last (minutes)? ____

tx.t: Here is some information about the Lantern Festival, which begins on the twenty-third of June. The gates open at quarter to eleven.

The first big event is the concert at quarter to six, on the green tent. Tickets for adults cost eighteen pounds, and children go free. If you bring children, there will be a treasure hunt on the grass next to the stage.
Parking is limited, so please use the north field. A free shuttle bus runs every fifteen minutes. We hope you enjoy the day.

qs.q: What time do the gates open? ____

tx.t: Thanks for your presentation on recycling in the local area, Maya. Overall it was good.
Thank you. What did you like most?
I really liked the clear structure. It showed that you had prepared well.
Was there anything I should improve?
One problem is that there was too much text on the slides. Next time, I suggest you use pictures and short phrases instead.
Was it the right length?
You spoke for sixteen minutes, but the limit was eleven, so you need to cut something. Your final presentation is on the eleventh of January.

you read from your notes too often

tx.t: Hello, Rachel. I wanted to talk about my essay, because I am having problems with writing a clear introduction.
That is quite common. My advice is to write the introduction last.
Thank you. How many articles should I read?
About eleven would be enough. Start with Chapter five of the course book.
And the word limit?
It is thirty-five hundred words. The deadline is next Monday, and I cannot accept late work.

qs.q: What is the student having problems with?

o: ask the librarian to help with a database search
write a one-sentence summary of each paragraph first
cut examples that repeat the same point

tx.t: We need to divide the work for our project. I could do the introduction because I have read most of the sources.
Good. I will take the slides. Sophie, what about you?
I would like to do the literature review, if nobody minds.
That is fine. When is the deadline for the first draft?
It is Friday. We should meet to check everything before that.
How about the student cafe at two o'clock the day before?
That works for me.

qs.q: Who will do the first task?
Who will do the second task?
Who will do the third task?
What is the deadline for the first draft?

tx.t: Hello Priya. Have you decided what to research for your project?
Yes. I would like to look at social media use among teenagers. I was thinking of using a diary study.
That has one clear advantage: you can collect information over a long period. But the problem is that participants often forget to complete it.
I see. What would you suggest instead?
I would try interviews. It would let you get detailed and personal answers, although they take a long time to arrange.
That sounds better. I think I will use that, with about twenty-seven participants.
Good. Remember that you need permission from the ethics committee, and you should finish collecting data by the twenty-eighth of August.
Understood. Thank you.

it is hard to find out why they do it
participants often forget to complete it
the results may not apply elsewhere

a signed letter from your supervisor

tx.t: Have you thought about where to take the class for the trip, Hannah?
I am torn between the botanical gardens and the city council offices.
What are the strengths of the botanical gardens?
Well, there are rare plants from many countries.
That is a strong point. And the city council offices?
Well, officials can explain how decisions are made, but it is much further away.

Then I would choose the botanical gardens, because it is nearer. We have twenty-two students, so book the coach early. It costs ten pounds each, and the coach should leave at eight o'clock on the fifth of December.

tx.t: Hello Priya. Have you decided what to research for your project?
Yes. I would like to look at attitudes to remote working. I was thinking of using a focus group.
That has one clear advantage: you can see how people react to each other. But the problem is that a few people may dominate the discussion.
I see. What would you suggest instead?
I would try observation. It would let you record what people really do, although it is hard to find out why they do it.
That sounds better. I think I will use that, with about twenty-six participants.
Good. Remember that you need written consent from each participant, and you should finish collecting data by the twenty-sixth of March.
Understood. Thank you.

tx.t: Today I will outline how solar power works and why its use is growing. Solar panels contain photovoltaic cells, which turn sunlight directly into electricity.
Most cells are made of silicon, the second most common element in the Earth's crust. The first practical silicon solar cell was made at Bell Laboratories in nineteen fifty-four.
A typical modern panel converts about twenty per cent of the sunlight that hits it into electricity. Over the last decade the cost of panels has fallen by about ninety per cent.
A panel usually works for about twenty-five years, although its output slowly declines.

qs.q: What are most solar cells made of?
When was the first practical silicon cell made?
How much sunlight does a typical panel convert (per cent)? ____
By how much has the cost fallen?
How long does a panel usually work (years)? ____

tx.t: The new Northam library opened in twenty thirteen, at a cost of twenty-eight million pounds. It has seven floors and holds more than two hundred and ninety thousand books.
Its most unusual feature is a children's theatre, which is used mainly for story-telling on Saturdays.
The library is open eighty-three hours a week, and membership is free for everyone who lives in the city.

qs.q: How much did it cost (millions of pounds)? ____
How many floors does it have? ____
What is its most unusual feature?
How many hours a week is it open? ____

tx.t: This morning we are going to look at some basic facts about the Moon. The Moon is about three hundred and eighty-four thousand kilometres from the Earth.
It takes about twenty-seven days to orbit the Earth once. The same side of the Moon always faces us, because its rotation takes exactly as long as its orbit.
The Moon is about a quarter of the width of the Earth. Gravity on the Moon is only about one-sixth of gravity on Earth.

qs.q: How far is the Moon from Earth (kilometres), roughly?
How many days does one orbit take? ____
Why does the same side always face Earth?
o: Its rotation takes as long as its orbit
It does not rotate at all
The Sun holds it in place

qs.q: How wide is the Moon compared with Earth?
How strong is lunar gravity compared with Earth?

tx.t: Today I would like to describe a bike-sharing scheme in the town of Calder. It began in twenty twelve with three hundred and six bikes, placed at stations around the centre.
Use grew quickly. Within three years the number of journeys had risen by thirty-eight per cent, and on a busy day there were more than twenty-seven thousand trips.
The scheme soon met a serious problem: theft and damage. The council solved it with a tracking system fixed inside each frame.
Today, a ride costs two pounds five for the first half hour, and the first fifteen minutes are free for residents.

qs.q: How many bikes were there at the start? ____
By how much did journeys rise in three years (per cent)? ____
What problem did the scheme meet?
o: bikes being left in the wrong places
too few bikes in the hills
a mobile app that shows where bikes are available
marked parking zones with a small fine for leaving a bike outside them
a van that moves bikes uphill every morning
a tracking system fixed inside each frame

qs.q: What does a ride cost for the first half hour?

tx.t: This week we are studying the life of Marie Curie, one of the most important scientists of the twentieth century. She was born in Warsaw in eighteen sixty-seven and moved to Paris to study when she was twenty-four.

Together with her husband Pierre, she discovered two new elements, polonium and radium, in eighteen ninety-eight. In nineteen oh three she won the Nobel Prize in Physics, becoming the first woman ever to win a Nobel Prize.
In nineteen eleven she won a second Nobel Prize, this time in Chemistry. During the First World War, she developed mobile X-ray units that doctors used to treat wounded soldiers.
She died in nineteen thirty-four, probably because of her long exposure to radiation.

qs.q: In which city was she born?
Which elements did she discover with her husband?
What was she the first woman to win?
In which subject was her second Nobel Prize?
What did she develop during the First World War?

Today, a ride costs two pounds thirty for the first half hour, and the first fifteen minutes are free for residents.

tx.t: In today's lecture we will study volcanoes and the damage they can do. There are around one thousand three hundred and fifty potentially active volcanoes in the world.

About three quarters of them lie around the Pacific Ocean, in an area called the Ring of Fire. In eighteen fifteen, Mount Tambora in Indonesia erupted so violently that the following year became known as the year without a summer.
The ash from large eruptions can block sunlight and cool the whole planet for a year or more. Scientists measure small earthquakes and gas emissions to try to predict eruptions.

qs.q: How many potentially active volcanoes are there, roughly?
What is the area around the Pacific called?

items.title: Ulugh Beg and the Samarkand Observatory

tx.t: Today I would like to tell you about Ulugh Beg, the ruler and astronomer of Samarkand. Ulugh Beg was a grandson of the conqueror Timur, and he ruled Samarkand in the first half of the fifteenth century.
He built a great observatory in Samarkand in the fourteen twenties. Its main instrument was a giant sextant, with a radius of about forty metres.
With it, his team made a catalogue of more than a thousand stars that was used for centuries. His measurement of the length of the year was wrong by less than a minute.

qs.q: When did he build the observatory?
How large was its radius, roughly (metres)? ____
How accurate was his measurement of the year?
o: Wrong by less than a minute

tx.t: Researchers at the University of Alderton carried out a study in twenty nineteen to find out how students prepare for exams. They followed two hundred and fifty-one students over five weeks.
On average, the students studied for six hours a day. However, only sixty-eight per cent of them used any planned method.
The students who used the method of studying at the same time each day felt less stressed before the exam. The researchers concluded that how you study may matter more than how long you study.

qs.q: Which institution carried out the study?
How long did the study last (weeks)? ____
How many hours a day did students study on average? ____

o: studying at the same time each day
studying in short sessions with breaks
